messages:
customer-ops: FYI customer (acme) escalated — intermittent partial SSE payloads, then client reconnects and gets the remainder but tokens are duplicated/misaligned. Path: Cloudflare -> NLB -> our origin. Happening across multiple regions. Request id: rc-9f3b. Any immediate triage steps?

alex: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and an example of the truncated output? Also how long between initial stream silence and client reconnect?

customer-ops: Repro curl below. The client disconnects after ~75s of silence and then reconnects immediately. Partial output example: first connect returns tokens up to "...response to your" then socket closes, reconnect returns "question. Additional tokens" so sentence broken.

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \  
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \  
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=gpt-open-2"

# client shows SSE data lines then stops; client reconnects and gets new SSE stream
```

maya: This smells like proxy idle/keepalive mismatch + buffering. Cloudflare and NLB/ALB have different idle timeouts + some proxies buffer chunked responses until a buffer threshold. Two quick checks: 1) tcpdump at origin to see if we send FIN/FIN-ACK or keep sending; 2) response headers for any buffering hints (e.g., cf-cache-status, x-amz-debug, x-envoy... ). Also check that we're flushing chunked frames (fflush or socket flush in runtime).

alex: Can you paste the last few bytes from origin-side tcpdump around the cutoff? Even a hexdump or tcp sequence will help determine if origin sent a FIN or data stop.

customer-ops: Snippet from origin tcpdump (redacted ip):

```
11:12:34.567890 IP 10.0.0.12.34567 > 10.0.1.8.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12512, ack 54321, win 501, length 167
  Payload: "data: {\"token\": \"...response to your\"}\n
11:13:49.890123 IP 10.0.0.12.34567 > 10.0.1.8.443: Flags [F.], seq 12512, ack 54321, win 501, length 0
  # FIN from origin after ~75s silence window
```

maya: That FIN is telling — origin side closed the connection. Could be our runtime deciding stream is done or an upstream keepalive handler. Do we see any 5xx or internal errors in logs around rc-9f3b?

eng-ml: Looking at model-serving logs for rc-9f3b: runtime emitted normal stream flushes every token but had an internal idle-snapshot GC at T+75s (we recently enabled an optimization that collapses idle KV caches and can trigger a graceful shutdown of long-idle sessions). This could send FIN. We should avoid sending FIN if there are outstanding SSE sessions — must switch to half-close semantics or keepalive pings.

sam: Meanwhile Cloudflare's default http keepalive idle is ~100s depending on plan; ALB is 60s, NLB is 350s. The smallest effective timeout in our path is ALB 60s (if present) or Cloudflare 100s. If origin sends FIN earlier than the proxy, the proxy may try to reestablish and the client reconnects, which can cause overlap/resumption issues. Workaround: send heartbeat comment lines every 15-30s so intermediaries see activity and won't idle-close. Also ensure Cloudflare "no-transform" headers to avoid buffering/coalescing.

customer-ops: Customer also reported billing spike from retries — reconnects create duplicate partial charges. They want a mitigation and a possible credit.

alex: For immediate mitigation: 1) push runtime change to disable idle-snapshot GC for SSE endpoints, 2) add a 20s heartbeat in the API gateway response path, 3) set Cache-Control: no-transform and Transfer-Encoding: chunked explicitly. Can someone open a quick rollback-safe patch?

eng-ml: I'll open a small rollbackable change to skip idle-snapshot for endpoints with Accept: text/event-stream. Also adding an explicit flush() call after each SSE chunk — that ensures bytes hit the socket and won't get coalesced by our runtime.

maya: Ops checklist for next 24h: - collect a few tcpdumps (origin + pre-origin proxy if possible) around multiple events - ask Cloudflare support to check for any transform/buffering on that route - set heartbeat to 20s in gateway as a config flag - document reconnection semantics with Last-Event-ID for clients so they can resume reliably.

customer-ops: Quick question: can we use Last-Event-ID for our generator streams? How would that look?

maya: Yes, SSE supports Last-Event-ID. We can emit an event id with each chunk (e.g., event: token
id: <sequence number>
data: {...}). On reconnect, client sends "Last-Event-ID: <seq>" header; server can fast-forward or re-synthesize tokens from KV cache. Example SSE chunk: 

```
event: token
id: 12345
data: {\"token\":\"hello\"}

: heartbeat
```

sam: Also add HTTP header `Cache-Control: no-transform, no-store` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (nginx) / `X-Proxy-Buffering: off` for other proxies where supported. Cloudflare respects `no-transform` for many transforms.

infra-bot: Cloudflare ticket created: #CF-89222 (customer rc-9f3b). Notified oncall.

alex: Next steps: eng-ml deploy skip-idle-snapshot for SSE (canary early tonight), add heartbeat config on gateway, ops to gather tcpdumps + CF reply, and customer-ops to propose billing credit once we confirm duplicate charges. I'll own the runbook entry for SSE proxy-idle issues.

customer-ops: Thanks — I'll tell the customer we have a mitigation path and will follow up with CF ticket id. Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
